text: Oakstead. An ordinary morning, as far as anyone knows.

speaker: Essa
text: You are not “just stepping out,” Kai. Last time you were “just stepping out,” you came back after dark with wet boots and somebody else’s goat.

speaker: Kai
text: The goat was having a difficult day.

speaker: Tam
text: The goat won.

speaker: Kai
text: Cruelly.

speaker: Essa
text: You laugh now. You still need willow bark, chanterelles if you find them, and if Old Mara asks, you are not climbing her roof again.

speaker: Kai
text: She asked me to last time.

speaker: Essa
text: She asks everyone to do things she should not ask.

speaker: Tam
text: She only asks the ones she thinks will say yes.

speaker: Kai
text: So I’m beloved. Good to know.

speaker: Essa
text: You’re useful. Don’t dress it up.

speaker: Kai
text: I’ll be home before the light goes.

speaker: Essa
text: That is what you said yesterday.

speaker: Kai
text: And look how confidently I’m saying it today.

speaker: Tam
text: Basket.
Tam nudges the basket toward him. It is already packed for the things Kai always forgets.

speaker: Tam
text: If you go beyond the ridge, at least pretend you thought better of it first.

speaker: Kai
text: I always pretend.

speaker: Essa
text: Kai.

speaker: Kai
text: Ma.

speaker: Essa
text: Home before dark.

speaker: Kai
text: One of these days, you’ll learn to ask me for something easy.

speaker: Essa
text: I did. I asked you to come home.
